segments.spokenText: Part 2. Tour of the Westfield recreation centre. You now have one minute to read questions 11 to 20.

Welcome to Westfield. I'll explain the rooms using the plan on your information sheet, then mention changes to our membership arrangements. You are standing at reception, shown at the bottom of the plan. The corridor runs straight towards the outdoor court at the top. Left and right refer to the direction you're facing now, not to somebody returning from the court. The central corridor stays clear; equipment should never be left there, even for a minute between classes.

segments.spokenText: The room immediately to your right is the equipment store. It has double doors, so returning larger items is easier. Members can borrow rackets there, but staff need to record the number before you take them outside. Please don't help yourself just because another customer has left the door open. Opposite, immediately to your left, is a staff room that is not open to members.

segments.spokenText: Walk towards the court and you'll reach two more rooms. The first on the left is the exercise studio. This is where stretching and low-impact classes take place. There are mirrors along one wall, but don't confuse it with the dance studio at our other building. Across the corridor, the first room on the right beyond the store is the changing area. There are accessible facilities within it, so you don't need to ask for a separate key at reception.

segments.spokenText: Continue to the last pair of rooms. On the left, just before the door to the court, is the first-aid room. It is staffed during all organised sessions. On the right is the meeting room, where club organisers can discuss events without standing in reception. That room used to contain vending machines. We've moved refreshments into the entrance area to free it for meetings and small training sessions.

segments.spokenText: Outdoor-court bookings are now released seven days ahead. Previously, some members reserved several weeks in advance and then cancelled shortly before playing, leaving little opportunity for others. The shorter window is intended to improve access. It isn't a response to resurfacing work; that was finished last month and doesn't affect the current schedule.

segments.spokenText: Equipment hire is included in the membership price for ordinary sessions. However, lost items must still be paid for. We don't want members to avoid trying a new sport because they haven't bought the right racket, but borrowing carries responsibility. If you find a defect before playing, show staff so that it isn't attributed to you when you return the item.

segments.spokenText: Our introductory classes have a new attendance rule. You may reserve a place without paying an extra class fee, but if you cannot come, cancel by the previous evening. Two unexplained absences in a month lead to a temporary booking restriction. The aim is to release unused places, not collect penalties from people whose circumstances change unexpectedly.

segments.spokenText: Children under twelve must be accompanied in the building, except when handed over to a registered children's class. An adult waiting in the café has not automatically completed that handover. Please speak to the class leader, who keeps a register. If you are collecting for another family, make sure the arrangement has been recorded before the session ends.

segments.spokenText: Finally, we are looking for feedback on quieter opening periods. We already know that Saturday morning is busy. What we need now is information from people who would use the centre at other times if a particular activity were offered. The short form asks about feasible times as well as preferred activities. A popular suggestion isn't useful if everyone who chooses it is unavailable when the room can actually be staffed.
